proposals.impact: convert quiz landing visits into starts
proposals.observation: In the 48-hour quiz window, one session reached intro_load and zero starts were recorded. The visitor landed, the page rendered, and nothing happened. That is a 0% start rate from a real human who found the quiz, which means the intro screen itself is the drop point. The source URL is a deploy preview, suggesting this may also be a Joel or team test, but the pattern holds regardless: the intro copy or CTA is not pulling the click.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro's primary CTA button text and the one or two sentences immediately above it. The current text (placeholder below) is almost certainly generic enough to apply to any quiz on any coaching site. Replace it with something only Joel could write, rooted in the gym-bag moment or the unopened tax-return tab, so the visitor reads a line that sounds like their own life and clicks because of recognition, not persuasion. One file, one component, the button label and its surrounding sentence.

proposals.impact: lift open rates on lower-performing automations
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Avoidance is at 52.63% across 19 sends. Money Worship sits at 37.5% across 16 sends. That 29-percentage-point gap between Vigilance and Worship is not noise across those send volumes. The Vigilance sequence is doing something structurally or tonally different in its subject lines or opening sentences that the Worship sequence is not. Identifying what that is and applying it to the Worship sequence is the highest-return email edit available right now.
proposals.proposal: Open both sequences side by side. Compare the subject line construction and the first sentence of email one in each. The Vigilance sequence almost certainly leads with a specific, recognisable tension ("you check your account three times before you spend £40") while the Worship sequence likely leads with a broader frame. Rewrite the Money Worship sequence email one subject line and opening sentence to match the specificity register of the Vigilance sequence, without copying its content. One file edit, email one only.
proposals.current_text:
Subject: Your relationship with money and success

Money worship is one of the most common money scripts in high earners. If you scored highly here, you likely believe that more money will solve your problems and that you can never have quite enough.
proposals.new_text:
Subject: The number that would finally make you feel okay

You have probably had a figure in your head for years. Not a goal exactly. More like a threshold. The point where the anxiety would quiet down and you could stop watching the account so closely. Most people who score high on money worship carry that number somewhere beneath every financial decision they make, and the number keeps moving.

proposals.impact: restore daily content output and stop queue drain
proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed in the last 24 hours: Daily Blog Post at 06:54 and Funnel-Hack Digest at 11:35. The content queue shows only one post queued against 47 published, meaning the pipeline is nearly empty and a workflow failure at this moment stops new content from reaching the site entirely. The Daily Blog Post failure is the more urgent of the two because it directly affects organic reach and the freshness signal for returning visitors.
proposals.proposal: Add a failure notification step to the Daily Blog Post workflow so that when the run fails, Joel receives an immediate alert (email or Slack, whichever is already wired) with the error output attached. This does not fix the underlying failure cause, but it closes the gap between failure and awareness, which right now appears to be the full overnight window. One file, one additional step block at the end of the on-failure path.
proposals.current_text:
- name: Commit new post
        run: |
          git config user.name "fred-bot"
          git config user.email "fred@wayofwealth.co.uk"
          git add src/content/blog/
          git commit -m "feat(content): daily blog post $(date +'%Y-%m-%d')" || echo "Nothing to commit"
          git push
proposals.new_text:
- name: Commit new post
        run: |
          git config user.name "fred-bot"
          git config user.email "fred@wayofwealth.co.uk"
          git add src/content/blog/
          git commit -m "feat(content): daily blog post $(date +'%Y-%m-%d')" || echo "Nothing to commit"
          git push

      - name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: dawidd6/action-send-mail@v3
        with:
          server_address: smtp.gmail.com
          server_port: 465
          username: ${{ secrets.NOTIFY_EMAIL_USER }}
          password: ${{ secrets.NOTIFY_EMAIL_PASS }}
          to: joel@wayofwealth.co.uk
          from: Fred (Way of Wealth CI) <fred@wayofwealth.co.uk>
          subject: "Daily Blog Post workflow failed — ${{ github.run_id }}"
          body: |
            The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at step: ${{ github.job }}.
            Run ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
            Triggered at: ${{ github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}
            Check the full log at: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
